title: Nondegeneracy of the restricted symplectic form
statement: Let $p$ be a prime, and equip $V = \bbf_p^n \times \bbf_p^n$ with the symplectic form $\omega\big((x,z),(x',z')\big) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(x_i z'_i - z_i x'_i)$. For any subset $M \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-1\}$, let $V_M$ be the support submodule consisting of those $(x,z) \in V$ with $x_i = z_i = 0$ for every $i \notin M$. Then the restriction of $\omega$ to $V_M$ is nondegenerate: if $u \in V_M$ satisfies $\omega(u,v) = 0$ for all $v \in V_M$, then $u = 0$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a subset (finite set) of the index set Fin n
replaced: The restricted symplectic form on $V_M$ is non-degenerate.
